items.bold: FACT CHECK: No confirmed Indian tanker crossing Hormuz on April 19.
items.text: VERIFIED: No credible source — CBS, NBC, Al Jazeera, Reuters, Republic World — confirms an Indian tanker successfully transited Hormuz on April 19. What IS confirmed: during the brief 24-hour Hormuz opening (Apr 17-18), at least 8 oil and gas tankers crossed (AFP/Al Jazeera). Some Indian-flagged vessels may have been among those 8+ ships in the brief window. However, the Indian-flagged VLCC carrying 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude was FIRED UPON by IRGC gunboats on April 18 and TURNED BACK — confirmed by UKMTO, Republic World, Reuters. As of April 19, Hormuz is CLOSED and IRGC is targeting all approaching vessels. India MEA summoned Iranian ambassador and urged Iran to resume facilitating India-bound ships — implying passage is NOT currently happening.

items.bold: India MEA official statement: deep concern, urged Iran to resume India-bound facilitation.

New Delhi urged Iran to "resume at the earliest the process of facilitating India-bound ships across the Strait." The ambassador "undertook to convey these views to the Iranian authorities." India was historically among nations Iran labelled "friendly" (along with China, Russia, Pakistan, Iraq). That preferential arrangement has broken down with the IRGC reclosure. The urging to "resume at the earliest" confirms India-bound ships are currently NOT transiting as of April 19.

FACT: No Indian tanker crossing Apr 19 confirmed — VLCC fired on Apr 18. Brent ~$97. Ceasefire Apr 22 — 3 days. Monday = defining day.
assessment.body:
Day 51 evening brings the most important diplomatic signal since the Hormuz crisis erupted.

THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FACT: US OFFICIALS GOING TO ISLAMABAD
• CBS News (updated within the hour): Trump says US officials travelling to Pakistan
• Talks could resume as soon as Monday — ceasefire expiry day itself
• No firm date, but direction of travel is clear: deal, not war
• Saturday Situation Room decision: Vance, Rubio, Hegseth, Ratcliffe, Witkoff all agreed — keep talking
• Senior US official: if no breakthrough soon, war could resume

THE NUCLEAR PROGRESS REVELATION (AXIOS)
• Axios (senior US official): "gaps narrowed on uranium enrichment and HEU BEFORE Hormuz crisis"
• Trump (Bloomberg): "Most main points finalized. Will go pretty quickly."
• Iran NOT confirmed — but structural progress is real per US side
• The Hormuz reclosure was tactical pressure over blockade, not nuclear breakdown
• Rubio civilian-nuclear concession (Apr 18) still stands
• This is why Trump is sending officials to Pakistan rather than resuming strikes

FACT CHECK: THE INDIAN TANKER STORY
• VERIFIED: No credible source confirms Indian tanker transiting Hormuz on April 19
• What happened during brief Apr 17-18 window: 8+ ships crossed (AFP confirmed)
• Indian VLCC (2M barrels Iraqi crude): FIRED ON by IRGC Apr 18, TURNED BACK
• India MEA (Misri) summoned Iran ambassador: urged Iran to "RESUME" India-bound facilitation
• The word "resume" explicitly confirms India-bound ships are NOT currently transiting
• Any reports of an Indian tanker crossing April 19 are UNVERIFIED

INDIA MEA POSITION
• Foreign Secretary Misri: deep concern expressed formally
• India urged Iran to resume India-bound ship facilitation at the earliest
• India-Iran back channel active — ambassador instructed to convey to Tehran
• India was among Iran's "friendly" five nations since March — arrangement broken
• Op Urja Suraksha warships on HIGH ALERT

BRENT AND MARKETS
• Brent ~$96-97 after partial recovery from Friday's $90 crash
• 19 ships turned back under US blockade total (CBS News confirmed)
• JPMorgan: pre-closure barrels fully exhausted from supply chain by ~April 20
• From Monday: world fully dependent on any new Hormuz transit
• ING: 13M bpd supply disrupted

MONDAY APRIL 21 — THE DEFINING DAY
• Ceasefire expires + India market opens + US officials possibly in Islamabad
• If talks restart + extension announced: Sensex 79,000-81,000+, Brent $80-88
• If no deal, ceasefire lapses: Sensex 74,000-76,000, Brent $108-118
• Infosys results Wednesday April 23 — domestic anchor amid storm
• India's five-week energy buffer being consumed daily

VERDICT: The US is going to Pakistan. Nuclear progress is real. The Hormuz crisis is negotiating theatre. The deal is close — but "close" in this war has meant many things before. Monday will tell. India's markets, rupee, energy costs, and 280 seafarers' safety all depend on what gets announced in the next 48 hours.
